authors: Tyukavina, A., Stehman, S.V., Foody, G.M., Bontemps, S., See, L., Olofsson, P. et al.
title: Land Cover and Change Map Accuracy Assessment and Area Estimation Good Practices Protocol, Version 1.1
source: CEOS WGCV Land Product Validation Subgroup, 187 pp.
relevance: The current authoritative community protocol, 187 pages, written by the same people whose individual papers Phase 4 assembled one at a time - Stehman, Foody, Olofsson, Radoux, Woodcock are all already in our tracker as IDs 69-76, 78-80 and 87. It consolidates that machinery and, critically for us, covers CHANGE maps specifically rather than single-date maps, which Search 49 showed is the quantity our numbers do not currently describe. This should be the document our accuracy reporting is written against; adopting a published community standard also makes our figures comparable to other work in a way a bespoke protocol never will be. Read it before finalizing the P3 design.

title: Impact of sample size allocation when using stratified random sampling to estimate accuracy and area of land-cover change
relevance: Poses a design choice our sample planning has never made explicit: allocation targeting USER'S ACCURACY of change is not effective for estimating the AREA of change, and vice versa - Neyman optimal allocation suits area and overall accuracy, equal allocation suits user's accuracy. Because change is rare, the change stratum is usually over-sampled, and which over-sampling rule you pick determines which question the sample can answer. We must decide whether P3 exists to say how accurate our change map is, or how much canopy actually changed. They are different studies and the loop has been treating them as one.
